text:
Sara: Heads-up — compliance flagged a bunch of nearly identical 'export ready' events being sent to SIEM when users spam the export button. It's inflating quotas and making downstream dedupe hard. Can we debounce/aggregate at the API layer?
Alex: +1. We should at least add an API-side debounce + an idempotency token. Suggestion: return the same export_id if the same user+tenant+payload within X seconds.
Mari: Important: we can't just drop events for audit purposes. The audit trail needs to reflect each user action (who clicked when). But we can emit a single export job and record the extra clicks as ancillary audit events.
Jordan: Right — splitting "action events" (UI clicks) vs "export jobs" is the key. The SIEM wants actionable export artifacts, but legal wants the click timeline. We should keep both but avoid reprocessing the export pipeline.
Sam: Ops saw a quota spike at 1711122100 from the export webhook fanout. ops-bot logged ~120 retries in 5m. If we debounce we also need to think about webhook retry/backpressure and presigned link churn.
ops-bot: NOTICE: export-webhook-service: 120 retries between 1711122100 and 1711122400; avg latency 3.2s — throttled to 10rps -> 503 on downstream.
Alex: Proposed config (proto):
```json
{"export_dedupe_window_ms": 30000, "export_idempotency_window_ms": 600000, "emit_click_audit": true}
```
Meaning: within 30s coalesce into 1 export job; keep idempotency mapping for 10min to return the same job id. Also write a lightweight click-audit record for each click.
Mari: That sounds reasonable. Click-audit record should be compact (actor, ts, button_context) so exports don't bloat. We should make the click-audit opt-in per tenant (some orgs want full click-forensics).
Jordan: Console UX: disable the export button after submit for 30s + show a toast "Export is queued — we'll notify you when ready". Also expose a small "recent exports" list in the modal so users see the job id and status (helps avoid re-click).
Sam: For downstream SIEM/EDR exports, we should add a header X-Redwood-Export-Canonical-Id so consumers can dedupe easily. Also include a field in the manifest like "duplicate_of": <canonical_id> when coalesced.
Alex: Edge-case: if the payload differs slightly (filter change) we should create a new job. So dedupe key = tenant + user + normalized payload hash.
Sara: Action items: Alex to spec API debounce and idempotency mapping; Mari to design minimal click-audit event shape & tenant opt flag; Jordan to mock console disable/UX; Sam to add webhook header + coord with downstreams.
Alex: I'll put a PR draft for the API change — will include metrics: number of coalesced clicks, number of new jobs, and SIEM events emitted per job.
Mari: Quick question — for compliance exports (legal hold) we should probably whitelist to disable dedupe so we preserve every job artifact. Flagging that as exception flow.
Sara: Agreed — add an "export_preserve_full_history": true tenant config for legal holds.
Jordan: Sounds good. If we can land a non-invasive debounce+click-audit in 2 sprints, we can reduce webhook churn and keep audit fidelity.
Sam: Will notify downstream teams about header change. Also, will add a small Dashboard panel showing "export churn" to monitor post-rollout.
Sara: Thanks all — let's move to the PR stage.
